Let \(a=BC\), \(b=CA\), \(c=AB\), and \(C=\angle ACB=\pi-\alpha-\beta=7\pi/12\).

By the sine rule, for some scale \(q\),
\[
a=q\sin\alpha,\quad b=q\sin\beta,\quad c=q\sin C.
\]
The area is
\[
S=\frac12(ak+bl+cm)
=\frac12 q\left(3\sin\frac{\pi}{6}+2\sin\frac{\pi}{4}+4\sin\frac{7\pi}{12}\right).
\]
Also,
\[
S=\frac12 ab\sin C=\frac12 q^2\sin\alpha\sin\beta\sin C.
\]
Equating gives
\[
S=\frac12\cdot
\frac{\left(3\sin\frac{\pi}{6}+2\sin\frac{\pi}{4}+4\sin\frac{7\pi}{12}\right)^2}
{\sin\frac{\pi}{6}\sin\frac{\pi}{4}\sin\frac{7\pi}{12}}.
\]
Now
\[
\sin\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac12,\quad 
\sin\frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{\sqrt2}{2},\quad
\sin\frac{7\pi}{12}=\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4}.
\]
So
\[
3\sin\frac{\pi}{6}+2\sin\frac{\pi}{4}+4\sin\frac{7\pi}{12}
=\frac32+2\sqrt2+\sqrt6,
\]
and
\[
\sin\frac{\pi}{6}\sin\frac{\pi}{4}\sin\frac{7\pi}{12}
=\frac{\sqrt3+1}{8}.
\]
Thus
\[
S=\frac12\cdot
\frac{\left(\frac32+2\sqrt2+\sqrt6\right)^2}
{\frac{\sqrt3+1}{8}}
=4\frac{\left(\frac32+2\sqrt2+\sqrt6\right)^2}{\sqrt3+1}
\approx 67.26.
\]
Rounded to the nearest whole number:
\[
\boxed{67}
\]
